description: Agent-DID HTTP verification vectors (RFC-001 §6.5): accepted and rejected requests. Each rejected vector differs from the valid one by a single change and is re-signed when that change touches signed material. Generated by scripts/regenerate-http-verification-vectors.js.
usage: For each vector: build the agent DID document from `keys` (every key is a verification method listed under its `relationships`), register it in a resolver, create a client whose clock returns `now` (the vector's own, else `clock`), and verify `request` with `headers` and a fresh nonce store whose own clock returns the same time.`expected` is the verdict and, for a rejection, `reason` is the `HttpSignatureRejection` a detailed verifier reports; `expectedSequence` is the sequence of verdicts (and `expectedReasons` the reasons, null for an accepted one) when the same request is verified repeatedly with ONE nonce store. `steps` is a sequence of verifications with ONE nonce store: each step verifies `request` with its own `headers` (else the vector's) at its own `now` (else the vector's, else `clock`), moving the clock of the client and of the store to that time, and states its own `expected` and, for a rejection, `reason`. Unless a vector gives its own, use the default verifier policy (skew 300 s, lifetime 300 s).
keysNote: TEST-ONLY Ed25519 keys. The seeds are public on purpose; they sign nothing real.

vectors.description: The baseline request: every rule holds.
A request without a query signs `@query` as `?`.
An explicit default port (:443) is dropped from `@authority`.
A non-default port stays in `@authority`.
Additional covered components MAY follow the seven required ones.

vectors.description: The `@signature-params` line is re-serialized from the parsed `Signature-Input`: extra spaces between the covered components do not change the signature base.
Header field names are matched case-insensitively.
No `Signature` header.
No `Signature-Input` header.
No `Agent-DID` header.
The rc.4 form: the DID as a bare `Signature-Agent` String covered as `"signature-agent"`, no `Agent-DID`. There is no legacy path.
No `Date` header (the signature covers it).
No `Content-Digest` header.
The body differs from the one `Content-Digest` was computed over.
`Content-Digest` uses `sha-512` instead of `sha-256`.
`Content-Digest` is a dictionary with `sha-256` and `sha-512`; the profile allows exactly one member, `sha-256`.
`tag="web-bot-auth"`: another profile must not be accepted as an Agent-DID signature.
No `tag` parameter.
`alg="ecdsa-p256-sha256"` on an Ed25519 signature.
No `alg` parameter.
No `nonce` parameter.
An empty `nonce`.
A `nonce` using every character class of the token grammar `[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]`.
A `nonce` of 256 characters, the maximum.
A `nonce` containing a space.
A `nonce` with a character outside the token grammar (`|`).
A `nonce` of 257 characters.
No `created` parameter.
No `expires` parameter.
No `keyid` parameter.
`now` is after `expires`.
`now` equals `expires`.
`created` is later than `now` by more than the allowed skew.
`created` is earlier than `now` by more than the allowed skew.
`created` is earlier than `now` by exactly the allowed skew.
`expires` is earlier than `created` while `now` is still before `expires`.
`expires - created` is 301 seconds with the default lifetime cap.
`expires - created` is exactly 300 seconds.
`keyid` is a key of another DID, not of the agent DID. The agent DID document even lists that key under assertionMethod and the signature is valid for it, so only the binding rule can reject it.
`keyid` names a fragment the agent DID document does not have.
`keyid` is a key listed only under `keyAgreement`, and the signature is valid for it.
The signature verifies under key-2, not under the `keyid` key-1.
The last byte of the signature is changed.
`Signature-Input` is not a Structured Field dictionary.
The `Agent-DID` field has a member for another label too; only the member of the signature's label counts.
`Agent-DID` carries the DID without a label, so it is not a Structured Field Dictionary.
`Agent-DID` has no member for the signature's label (`sig2` instead of `sig1`).
The member is a Token (`sig1=did:webvh:...`), not a String. Re-signed, so only the member type rule can reject it.
The member has a parameter (`sig1="did:...";v=1`). Re-signed, so only the parameter rule can reject it.
The `Agent-DID` member is replaced with another DID after signing; `keyid` is not a key of that DID.
The signature covers the whole `"agent-did"` field instead of `"agent-did";key="sig1"`.
The signature `sig1` covers `"agent-did";key="sig0"`, the member of another label.
The signature does not cover `"@method"`.
The signature does not cover `"@authority"`.
The signature does not cover `"@path"`.
The signature does not cover `"@query"`.
The signature does not cover `"content-digest"`.
The signature does not cover `"date"`.
The signature does not cover `"agent-did";key="sig1"`.
Two required components are swapped (`@path` before `@authority`).
The seven required components in reverse order.
An additional component comes before the required ones; additional components may only follow.

The same request is verified twice with one nonce store: the second `(keyid, nonce)` is a replay.
One nonce store: a forged request with the nonce of the valid one is rejected, then the valid request is accepted (the forged one did not record the pair), then the valid request again is a replay.
One nonce store: the request is accepted at `clock`, and the same request at `now == expires`, still within its validity (see `accept-at-expires`), is a replay: the pair is kept through `expires`.
